_about: DRAFT options.json (WEB, 2026-10-20, NEXT-WEB 106). WORDING, CONTROL TYPE AND DEFAULTS ONLY. It is NEVER the validator: every value, from a menu, the desktop app or a connected AI, passes the same server-side schema check before anything renders (CC1 13:27). Field paths are the engine's profile schema (tests/fixtures/profile.schema.json: look.*, pacing.*, reserved.*) and ENGINE's frozen clarity names (clarity-option-a 365d0e6, unmerged). ENGINE owns the fields, WEB owns the wording. status: built = the engine accepts it today; planned = named but not built or not merged; reserved = stored, not applied yet. hard = limits the server enforces; soft = a warning only, for taste (never size, time, render caps, rate limits or credits). VERSION 1 (NEXT-WEB 117, 2026-10-20): the 34 profile rows plus RENDERER's 128 engine story rows (their plain labels kept; WEB wrote the 70 advanced labels and help) and 10 gap rows. source: profile = a look or pacing field (the editor and the saved looks); story = a field of the story itself. same_as: the story row a profile row compiles into (the story field wins when both are set: ENGINE to confirm). connector: yes = the connected AI can set it through the connector (the server check stays the validator); no = not accepted today. help_detail = RENDERER's long viewer's-eye help (changes, use_when, example, careful) for a connected AI to read out; ENGINE-TO-CONFIRM items stay marked there.

groups.label: Size and speed
groups.help: How big the film is and how it moves.

groups.label: Words on screen
groups.help: The question and key a viewer reads first.

groups.label: Coming later
groups.help: Shown greyed out, with who is building it.

groups.label: Chart
groups.help: What the chart shows and how.

groups.label: The film
groups.help: Name, data and years: chosen when the film is made.

groups.label: Channel and credit
groups.help: Channel name, handle and credit line.

groups.label: Advanced
groups.help: Shown only when a chart type needs it.

chart_type.changes: Which picture the film draws: a map, bars (a ranking race), a line, a map beside a bar race (paired), a panel, or stacked shares.
chart_type.use_when: Map for 'where', bars for 'who is biggest', line for 'how did it change over time', shares for 'what is it made of'.
chart_type.example: Film 4 and Film 6 are maps; the biggest-cities film is a bar race.
chart_type.careful: Each type has its own limits (the living-map view has no vertical layout yet).

years.use_when: To cut a longer dataset to the years you want to tell.
years.careful: A year with no published data cannot be shown; the engine checks that the years you ask for exist.

hold_per_year.changes: How long each year stays on screen before the next.
hold_per_year.use_when: Longer on the years that matter (a peak or a collapse), shorter elsewhere.
hold_per_year.example: Two seconds a year, slowing to three on the turns in the housing film.
hold_per_year.careful: Too fast and a viewer cannot take in the change; too slow and the film drags.

bars_count.changes: How many bars are on screen: the top 1 to 20.
bars_count.use_when: Ten is a good default; fewer for a short film.
bars_count.careful: More bars make the names small.

bars_scale.changes: Whether the bars' scale stays fixed for the whole film or follows the data as it grows.
bars_scale.use_when: Fixed shows real growth; dynamic keeps the biggest bar always full width.
bars_scale.example: Fixed, so a city that doubles visibly doubles.
bars_scale.careful: A fixed scale starts small if the data grows a lot.

rate_or_count.changes: Whether the bars show a rate (per person) or a count.
rate_or_count.use_when: A rate when places differ a lot in size; a count when size is the point.
rate_or_count.example: Permits per 1,000 residents, not raw permits.
rate_or_count.careful: The film's title and key must say which one it is.

cards.rows: clip.title.headline, clip.title.subhead, clip.title.credit, clip.title.seconds, clip.title.fade, clip.title.align
cards.changes: The text cards before and after the data: a headline, a subhead, a credit, how long they stay and how they fade.
cards.use_when: An opening card that says what the film is, and a closing card that says what to remember.
cards.example: Film 6 opens on 'Boom, Bust and Back'.
cards.careful: A card has a reading-speed limit (about 250 words a minute) and a length limit, so long text is refused; claims on a card must match the facts file.

chart_subtitle.changes: The line under the chart title that changes with the story, for example '2009: 1.9 per 1,000, the floor'.
chart_subtitle.example: '2005: 7.4 per 1,000, the most homes permitted per person in the run.'
chart_subtitle.careful: Up to 200 characters; any number in it must match the data.

closing_card.changes: How long the Ryagram closing card stays (5 to 20 seconds) and one short line on it.
closing_card.use_when: Every film ends on it; change the line to point to your next film.
closing_card.careful: The Ryagram credit stays on every film.

channel_brand.changes: Your channel name, handle, credit line and logo on the closing card.
channel_brand.careful: A logo must be an uploaded file.

callouts.changes: A short note that appears beside a place at a chosen year, with its source.
callouts.use_when: To point at something the viewer should not miss.
callouts.example: '1900: Columbus had 125,560 residents, Dayton 85,333.' with the Census source.
callouts.careful: Every callout needs a source; up to 12 per scene; it must not cover the data, and it appears and leaves on a timer.

declared_stills.changes: Years you tell the engine are meant to hold still, so a deliberate pause is not mistaken for a stuck film.
declared_stills.use_when: When a year is a pause by design, such as a hold on a peak.
declared_stills.example: The 2009 floor held for three seconds.
declared_stills.careful: Up to 8; each is a year, a length and a reason.

line_chart.changes: The settings of a line chart: how many lines, the top of the scale, and a shaded band for a range.
line_chart.example: A shaded band marking the 2007 to 2009 recession.

network_roads.changes: The road-network film: the base layer, context roads, how roads are revealed and the route shields.
network_roads.example: Interstate shields drawn along each route as it opens.
network_roads.careful: Advanced and specific to that film.

shares.changes: The stacked-shares chart: which groups, their order, their colours and how many decimals.
shares.use_when: For 'what is it made of' films.
shares.example: Housing permits by building size: one unit, two to four, five or more.
shares.careful: Colours must stay clearly apart; the shares must add up to the whole.

frame_pacing.changes: How smoothly each year is drawn, how long the final picture holds, and how years are grouped.
frame_pacing.use_when: Rarely; the film's defaults are tuned.
frame_pacing.example: More pictures per year for a very slow, smooth map.
frame_pacing.careful: Advanced; more pictures means a longer, heavier render.

options.label: Page
options.help: Dark or light page behind the film. Dark is the default.

help_detail.changes: The page behind the whole film: near-black (dark) or white (light). Text and map colours flip with it.
help_detail.use_when: Dark is the default and the look every Ryagram film so far uses. Choose light only for a white-page setting, such as a slide that will be printed or placed on a white website.
help_detail.example: Film 6 (new homes approved by state) is dark; the early Film 4 was light.
help_detail.careful: A colour ramp that looks good on one page can fail on the other; the engine checks that the lowest colour stands apart from the page.

options.label: Page colour
options.help: Leave blank to use the page's own colour.

help_detail.changes: The exact colour of the page. Blank keeps the look's own page.
help_detail.use_when: Only to match a brand colour. Most films should leave it blank.
help_detail.example: A near-black blue page for a channel whose logo sits on that blue.
help_detail.careful: A very bright page makes the map's low colours hard to see; the quiet text colour must still be readable on it.

options.label: Quiet text colour
options.help: Source lines and small print.

help_detail.changes: The colour of the small print: sources, footnotes and secondary labels.
help_detail.use_when: Rarely. Change it only if the small print is hard to read on your page colour.
help_detail.example: A lighter grey for the source line on a very dark page.
help_detail.careful: Too close to the page and the source line becomes unreadable, which is a credit problem as well as a looks problem.

options.label: Map colour for low values
options.help: The colour of the lowest numbers.
options.note: ENGINE's dark-ramp rule refuses a low colour too close to the page; the page shows the engine's own sentence

help_detail.changes: The map colour of the lowest numbers.
help_detail.use_when: When the default colours do not suit the subject. Pick colours that suggest the subject (warm for heat, cool for cold).
help_detail.example: Film 6 uses a deep violet (#5b3f66) for the lowest permit counts.
help_detail.careful: On a dark page the lowest colour must stand clearly apart from the page and from the no-data grey, or low values will look like nothing. The engine refuses a colour that is too close and says so in a sentence.

options.label: Map colour for high values
options.help: The colour of the highest numbers.

help_detail.changes: The map colour of the highest numbers.
help_detail.use_when: Together with the low colour, to match the subject.
help_detail.example: Film 6 uses a pale cream (#ffe9b8) for the highest permit counts, so the busiest places glow.
help_detail.careful: Keep it clearly different from the low colour; for a two-sided scale (above and below an average) the middle colour matters too.

options.label: Map fill
options.help: WORDING TO CONFIRM WITH ENGINE: what 'hatch' looks like to a viewer.

help_detail.changes: Whether each colour band is a flat colour (solid) or a line pattern (hatched).
help_detail.use_when: Solid is the everyday choice. Hatched marks bands with a pattern so they stay apart when colours are close, or in black and white. ENGINE-TO-CONFIRM: the exact viewer look of hatch.
help_detail.example: The housing-supply map draws its bands from light to dark purple, with a separate hatched swatch for counties with no permit office.
help_detail.careful: Hatching is drawn as pictures, so it is only available in the vector look; it is not a smooth colour scale.

options.label: Smooth colours
options.help: Colours blend smoothly instead of in bands.

help_detail.changes: Colours blend smoothly from low to high instead of stepping in bands.
help_detail.use_when: When you want the picture to move: on a smooth scale a county changes colour a little every frame, so the film visibly flows.
help_detail.example: Film 6 uses smooth colours and moves all the way through; a banded map changes only when a county crosses a band, so long stretches look still.
help_detail.careful: A banded map often fails the engine's "does the film actually move" check (the housing-supply sheet did: only about 40% of frames changed against a 90% floor). Smooth colours cost the exact band labels.

options.label: Hatch line colour
options.help: Only used when the map fill is hatched.

help_detail.changes: The colour of the hatch lines.
help_detail.use_when: Only when the map fill is hatched.
help_detail.example: A light line on a dark band.
help_detail.careful: It must show against every band colour it sits on.

options.label: Dot colour
options.help: Places drawn as dots.

help_detail.changes: The colour of the dots on a dot map.
help_detail.use_when: When places are drawn as dots rather than filled areas.
help_detail.example: Amber for single-family homes in the housing dot test.
help_detail.careful: Dots of different kinds must stay clearly apart, also for colour-blind viewers; the engine checks the gap between classes.

options.label: Dot colour at the start
options.help: Where a dot starts from.

help_detail.changes: The colour of dots counted at the starting year.
help_detail.use_when: When you want to show new dots against the ones that were already there.
help_detail.example: Grey baseline dots, then coloured dots for the new ones.
help_detail.careful: Choose a baseline that sits quietly behind the new colour.

options.label: Dot size
options.help: Bigger dots are easier to see on a phone.

help_detail.changes: How big each dot is.
help_detail.use_when: Bigger for phones and small screens, smaller when the map is crowded.
help_detail.example: A larger dot for a Shorts version that will be watched on a phone.
help_detail.careful: Too big and dots overlap and hide each other; the engine checks that a dot is mostly its own colour.

options.label: Place fill
options.help: The fill of places with data.

help_detail.changes: The colour of places that have data but no colour of their own yet.
help_detail.use_when: Rarely; the map's colours normally cover it.
help_detail.example: A neutral dark grey for the land before the data fades in.
help_detail.careful: Keep it clearly different from the no-data colour so the two do not read as the same thing.

options.label: No-data colour
options.help: Places with no number for the year.

help_detail.changes: The colour of places with no number for that year.
help_detail.use_when: When the default grey is hard to tell apart from your low colour or the page.
help_detail.example: Film 4 draws the Connecticut areas that are not shown in a warm grey (#c4bfb7) so they cannot be mistaken for a low value.
help_detail.careful: If this colour matches another status colour (for example 'not shown' and 'not applicable') the engine fails the film, because a viewer cannot tell them apart.

options.label: Outline thickness
options.help: The line around each place. 0 hides it.

help_detail.changes: The thickness of the line around each state or county. 0 hides it.
help_detail.use_when: Thicker for a map of states, thinner or zero for a crowded county map.
help_detail.example: 1 pixel on the county maps.
help_detail.careful: A thick outline on thousands of small counties hides the colours.

options.label: How fast bars swap places
options.help: Seconds a bar takes to move when its rank changes.

help_detail.changes: How long a bar takes to move when it passes another.
help_detail.use_when: Shorter for a lively race, longer for a calm one.
help_detail.example: Half a second is the film default.
help_detail.careful: When many bars change places in one year, the moves happen one after another; a longer swap makes a cluster take longer and keeps the order and the printed numbers apart for longer (Ryan's Q139).

options.label: Space for names
options.help: Width of the name column, in pixels. Advanced.

help_detail.changes: How much room the names get on a bar chart.
help_detail.use_when: Wider if a name is cut off.
help_detail.example: A wider column for 'Los Angeles-Long Beach'.
help_detail.careful: Advanced: a very wide name column shrinks the bars.

options.label: Space for numbers
options.help: Width of the number column, in pixels. Advanced.

help_detail.changes: How much room the numbers get at the end of a bar.
help_detail.use_when: Wider for big numbers.
help_detail.example: A wider column for population counts in the millions.
help_detail.careful: Advanced.

options.label: Size
options.help: Widescreen for YouTube; vertical for Shorts.

choices.label: Vertical for Shorts (1080 x 1920)
choices.note: the schema accepts it but a true vertical layout is not built yet (ENGINE profile note); BUILDER's vertical work; show greyed with 'not ready yet'

help_detail.changes: The shape of the picture: widescreen (YouTube), 720p, or vertical (Shorts).
help_detail.use_when: Widescreen for YouTube; vertical for Shorts and phone-first posts.
help_detail.example: Film 4 is 1920x1080; the Shorts drafts are 1080x1920.
help_detail.careful: A vertical picture needs its own layout; not every chart type has one yet, and the engine refuses a vertical film that is not laid out for it.

options.label: Smoothness
options.help: Frames per second. 30 is smooth; 24 looks more like cinema.

help_detail.changes: How many pictures are drawn each second.
help_detail.use_when: 30 is smooth and is the default; 24 looks like cinema.
help_detail.example: All our films use 30.
help_detail.careful: Fewer frames per second means each year's change takes fewer pictures, so changes look steppier.

options.label: Pause at the end
options.help: How long the last picture stays on screen.

soft.text: A pause over 2 seconds can feel long. You can keep it.

help_detail.changes: How long the last picture stays on screen at the end.
help_detail.use_when: Long enough to read the final number and the source line.
help_detail.example: A second and a half for the final hold.
help_detail.careful: Too short and a viewer cannot read the last frame.

options.label: Between scenes
options.help: How one scene gives way to the next.

help_detail.changes: How one scene gives way to the next: a hard cut, a crossfade or a fade through black.
help_detail.use_when: A crossfade for a gentle change between a card and the chart.
help_detail.example: A 0.7-second crossfade between the map scenes in the housing film.
help_detail.careful: Long fades eat into the time a card has to be read.

options.label: Scene change length
options.help: Seconds the change takes.

help_detail.changes: How long the change between scenes takes.
help_detail.use_when: Short for a brisk film.
help_detail.example: 0.7 seconds.
help_detail.careful: Up to 3 seconds; longer is not allowed.

options.label: Title fade
options.help: Seconds the title card fades in.

help_detail.changes: How long the title card takes to fade in.
help_detail.use_when: A short fade for a clean open.
help_detail.example: 0.3 seconds on our title cards.
help_detail.careful: Keep it short so the words are readable as soon as they appear.

options.label: Title position
options.help: Centre or left.

help_detail.changes: Whether the title text is centred or left-aligned.
help_detail.use_when: Centre is the default; left suits a long headline.
help_detail.example: Left-aligned for a three-line headline.
help_detail.careful: Cards are limited in length so the text stays readable at the film's reading speed.

options.label: Question under the title
options.help: The one question this film answers, up to 120 characters. It stays on screen.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: Adds one line under the title that states the question the film answers, and keeps it on screen the whole time.
help_detail.use_when: Always, for a data film: it tells a viewer what they are looking at from the first second.
help_detail.example: Film 4: which counties got richer than the U.S. average, and which fell behind.
help_detail.careful: Planned (ENGINE clarity-option-a, not yet merged). Up to 120 characters; keep it a question or a plain statement, not a slogan.

options.label: A line of detail
options.help: Optional, under the question.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: An optional second line of detail under the question.
help_detail.use_when: To say what the colours or the measure mean.
help_detail.example: 'Blue is above the U.S. average, orange is below.'
help_detail.careful: Planned. Keep it short.

options.label: How fast the data fades in
options.help: 0 turns the fade off.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: How quickly the data fades in from a plain map at the start. 0 turns it off.
help_detail.use_when: Leave it short (about half a second) so the data appears smoothly but never abruptly.
help_detail.example: Film 4 uses 0.6 seconds: the map starts plain, and the first year's colours fade in over 18 frames.
help_detail.careful: Planned. With the fade on, the film is that many frames longer, because the fade happens before the first year is shown; every year from the first is drawn at full strength.

options.label: The colour key
options.help: 2 to 8 marks along the colour bar, each with a plain label.
options.note: stops are increasing and each inside the colour ramp's own range; the page shows the engine's sentence when refused
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: The colour key: a bar under the map with 2 to 8 marks and a plain label on each.
help_detail.use_when: Always on a map: it is how a viewer reads a colour as a number.
help_detail.example: Film 4's key reads from below to above the U.S. average.
help_detail.careful: Planned. Labels must stay readable and must not collide; the engine checks the key fits.

options.label: Music
options.help: A track under the film. Needs the audio block merged and a licence answer for uploads.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: A music track under the film.
help_detail.use_when: For a finished film; the track and its licence are part of the film's record.
help_detail.example: Film 4's track and mix are recorded in a music receipt.
help_detail.careful: Planned. Needs the audio block merged and a licence answer.

options.label: Captions
options.help: Burned-in captions and a .srt file.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: Burned-in captions and a caption file.
help_detail.use_when: When the film has speech or a voice-over.
help_detail.example: Open captions on a Short.
help_detail.careful: Planned.

options.label: Use each year's borders
options.help: Switch a map to the borders of each year, for example Connecticut's counties then planning regions.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: At the right date, the map switches to the borders of that year.
help_detail.use_when: When places change: Connecticut moved from 8 counties to 9 planning regions in 2024; Europe and Asia have more such changes.
help_detail.example: A county map that uses the old Connecticut counties up to 2023 and the new regions from 2024.
help_detail.careful: Planned/partly built (time-varying geography, on main for Connecticut). The frame where both sets of places exist needs plain words (Q135), and values across the switch are not comparable unless the film says so.

options.label: Fonts
options.help: Stored, not applied yet.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: The typeface used on the film.
help_detail.use_when: To match a brand.
help_detail.example: Your channel's font.
help_detail.careful: Stored, not applied yet.

options.label: Channel name and credit line
options.help: Stored, not applied yet.
options.connector_note: not built or not applied yet

help_detail.changes: Your channel name and credit line on the closing card.
help_detail.use_when: On every film you publish.
help_detail.example: 'Made with Ryagram' with your channel name.
help_detail.careful: Stored, not applied yet; the engine's own Ryagram mark stays on the closing card.

options.label: Film engine
options.help: Which drawing engine makes the film. It is always the sequence engine today; leave it.

options.label: Film name
options.help: Short name for the project (letters, numbers, dashes).

options.label: Notes
options.help: Your own notes; never drawn.

options.label: Story format version
options.help: The version of the story format. It is always 1; leave it.

options.label: Size
options.help: Frame size: 1920x1080, 1280x720 or vertical 1080x1920.

options.label: Scenes
options.help: The scenes of the film in order: title cards and charts. From 1 to 40.

options.label: Card alignment
options.help: Centre or left.

options.label: Card credit
options.help: A small credit under the card.

options.label: Card fade
options.help: Seconds the card fades in and out.

options.label: Card headline
options.help: The big line on a card.

options.label: Title card name
options.help: A short name for this title card, only so scenes can be told apart. Up to 40 characters.

options.label: Scene type: title card
options.help: Marks this scene as a title card.

options.label: Card length
options.help: Seconds the card stays on screen.

options.label: Card subhead
options.help: The line under the headline.

options.label: Between scenes
options.help: Cut, crossfade or fade.

options.label: Between-scenes length
options.help: Seconds the change takes.

options.help: Which dataset the scene draws.

options.label: Last year
options.help: Last period shown.

options.label: First period of this chart
options.help: The first year (or month) this chart shows. Leave blank to use the film's own start.

options.label: Hold on each year
options.help: Seconds each year stays before moving on.

options.label: Chart name
options.help: A short name for this chart scene, only so scenes can be told apart. Up to 40 characters.

options.label: Scene type: chart
options.help: Marks this scene as a chart.

options.label: Last period of this chart
options.help: The last year (or month) this chart shows.

options.label: Bar scale
options.help: Fixed or following the data.

options.label: Notes on the chart
options.help: Short written notes that appear at a chosen moment, each with its place, how long it stays and, if you like, its source. Up to 12.

options.label: When the note appears
options.help: The year (or month) at which this note shows.

options.label: Place the note points to
options.help: The place or item this note is about, for example a state name. Up to 40 characters.

options.label: Note name
options.help: A short name for this note, only so notes can be told apart. Up to 40 characters.

options.label: Shaded band: from

options.label: Shaded band: top value
options.help: The top of the band, in the chart's own units.

options.label: Shaded band: label
options.help: The words shown on the band, such as 'Recession'. Up to 120 characters.

options.label: Shaded band: to
options.help: The last year of the band.

options.label: Shaded band: bottom value
options.help: The bottom of the band, in the chart's own units. It must not be above the top.

options.label: How many lines to show
options.help: How many places a line chart draws, from 1 to 20.

options.label: Rate or count
options.help: Rate or count.

options.label: Road groups open at the start
options.help: Groups of roads drawn from the first frame as the starting network. Up to 6.

options.label: Label for the starting roads
options.help: The words for the roads already there at the start. Up to 120 characters.

options.label: When background roads appear
options.help: The year the background road layer fades in.

options.label: Background road types
options.help: Which kinds of road the background layer draws. Up to 5.

options.label: Background roads credit
options.help: The source credit shown for the background layer. Up to 200 characters.

options.label: Background roads fade
options.help: Seconds the background layer takes to fade in, from 0.1 to 10.

options.label: Background roads label
options.help: The words for the background layer in the key. Up to 120 characters.

options.label: Background roads data
options.help: Which road dataset the background layer comes from: primary and secondary roads (TIGER) or the National Highway Planning Network.

options.label: Counter label

options.label: How new roads appear
options.help: Roads appear mile by mile ('milepost') or fade in whole ('fade').

options.label: Where each period sits
options.help: Whether a period's number marks its end or its start.

options.label: Years per step
options.help: How many years one step of the film covers, from 1 to 10.

options.label: Colours of the groups
options.help: A colour for each group in a shares chart. Up to 30.

options.label: Decimal places in shares
options.help: How many decimals the percentages show, from 0 to 3.

options.label: Group names
options.help: The groups a shares chart is made of. Up to 12.

options.label: Order of the groups
options.help: The stacking order of the groups, bottom to top. It must name every group. Up to 30.

options.label: Shares as percent or count
